sights.w: NYC's third-largest park: 1,100+ acres of old forest, a freshwater lake, a 1748 stone manor and the nation's first public golf course.

sights.address: Bruckner Blvd & Westchester Ave, Bronx, NY 10461
sights.w: The city's largest park at 2,700+ acres: salt marsh, hiking trails, a lagoon, a bird sanctuary and the crescent of Orchard Beach.

sights.address: University Ave & W 170th St, Bronx, NY 10452
sights.w: NYC's oldest standing bridge (1848), a stone-arch former aqueduct reopened in 2015 as a pedestrian walkway across the Harlem River.
Free nonprofit photography and film gallery in Melrose mounting documentary exhibitions on social justice and the borough itself.
The apartment tower where DJ Kool Herc's August 1973 rec-room party gave birth to hip hop; state-recognized as the culture's birthplace.
A 1758 fieldstone farmhouse, the borough's second-oldest building, run as the Museum of Bronx History by the county historical society.
Riverfront greenway on the Bronx River where rusted 1940s concrete-batching towers were preserved as monumental industrial sculpture.
Weekend museum in an 1897 schoolhouse chronicling City Island's shipbuilding, oystering and America's Cup yacht-racing history.
Indoor market La Guardia built in 1940, packed with Italian butchers, cheesemongers, pasta stalls and hand-rolled cigars.

sights.address: E 161st St & Grand Concourse, Bronx, NY 10451
sights.w: Free open-air food festival near Yankee Stadium gathering 50+ local vendors on select spring and fall dates; seasonal, check the schedule.

food.w: Michelin-listed Albanian restaurant-museum off Arthur Avenue serving mountain-village cooking amid 18th-century folk artifacts.
Since 1959 a beloved Pelham Bay corner pizzeria turning out paper-thin New York pies topped with fennel-laced butcher's sausage.
East Tremont lechonera roasting dozens of whole hogs weekly for crackling-skinned pernil piled over garlicky mashed-plantain mofongo.
Cash-only waterfront City Island seafood shack famous for cafeteria trays of deep-fried shrimp, calamari and whiting by the Sound.
Three-generation Sicilian bakery on Arthur Avenue filling crackling cannoli shells to order, plus lard bread and prosciutto loaves.
Bronx Little Italy's oldest pastry shop (1912), cases glinting with flaky sfogliatelle, rainbow cookies and espresso at marble tables.

food.dish: brown-stew oxtail with rice and peas
food.w: Jamaican kitchen near Yankee Stadium, once on Bourdain, ladling brown-stew oxtail, curry goat and jerk chicken to a takeout crowd.
Grand Concourse storefront and Ghanaian community hub serving smoky jollof rice, fufu and goat light soup amid weekend soccer matches.
Big Schuylerville Cuban spot from chef Alex Garcia, known for garlicky green-plantain mofongo crowned with shrimp and pork chicharrón.
